It's arranged logically: overview, available containers, quick start, production, config, reverse proxy, plugins, cert, offline, swarm. Maybe good. - Quick start: `SECRET_KEY_BASE` explained. It says will see success message indicating default admin password (login admin password admin). Actually success message? Maybe logs.
- In quick start, `OPENPROJECT_DEFAULT__LANGUAGE=en` included first command but omitted in daemonized command. That's okay.
- Production command omits `OPENPROJECT_HTTPS=false`, which means HTTPS mode enabled by default. They set `OPENPROJECT_HOST__NAME=openproject.example.com`; if no TLS termination, will not work? They mention external proxy and TLS. But the command doesn't include `OPENPROJECT_HTTPS=false`; production expects HTTPS. It also doesn't map? It maps 8080:80. They should configure reverse proxy. Fine.
- Self-signed cert first command has comments after backslash: `--mount ... \ #mount my_root.crt to /tmp` this is invalid shell because backslash followed by space and comment? Let's examine:
```
sudo docker run -it -p 8080:80 \
  -e SECRET_KEY_BASE=<your-secret-key-base> \
  -e OPENPROJECT_HOST__NAME=localhost:8080 \
  -e OPENPROJECT_HTTPS=false \
  -e OPENPROJECT_DEFAULT__LANGUAGE=en \
  --mount type=bind,source=$(pwd)/my_root.crt,target=/tmp/my_root.crt \ #mount my_root.crt to /tmp
  -e SSL_CERT_FILE=/tmp/my_root.crt \ #set the SSL_CERT_FILE to the path of my_root.crt
  openproject/openproject:17
```
This is invalid due comments after backslash. The backslash escapes the space? Actually in shell, `\ #`? Let's parse: backslash at end before space? line has `\ #mount`; backslash escapes the following space, so ` #mount` becomes literal space + #? Wait a backslash followed by space prevents space from separating words, then # is not at start of word? It may be part of argument? Actually ` \ #comment`: backslash escapes space, so ` ` becomes literal space in current word? Then `#` is not at beginning of word because preceded by escaped space? It might be part of argument? Let's test mentally: `echo foo \ #bar` -> echo foo  #bar? Hmm. Backslash-newline is line continuation; here backslash before space not newline, so it escapes space, making space part of next word? Then `#` not at start? It could cause a filename " #mount"? Then next line `-e` becomes separate command. So invalid. This is clarity issue. Also offline section has `openproject-12.tar.gz` instead of 17 or stable, inconsistent. It says "latest OpenProject docker image" but saves 17; load uses 12. This is an error. Structure maybe minor. Clarity: some inconsistencies and outdated references (postgres:13 vs postgres:10, openproject-12). The Swarm section uses `openproject/openproject:17` and postgres:13 then postgres:10 in scaling output. Inconsistencies. The guide is generally clear but has these errors. Score 4? Or 3? Need identify.

Understandability: Mostly easy, explains terms (slim, all-in-one, tags, env vars). Some advanced sections (Swarm, reverse proxy) assume networking knowledge but that's acceptable. It explains Docker prerequisite. Technical terms like HSTS, X-Forwarded-Proto, load balancer are somewhat explained but not all. For target, perhaps adequate to good. Score 4.
